authority.requirement: Worker scheduling gives indexing, importing, grading and recommendations bounded rounds; no long write lock or unbounded loop is a reliable scheduling claim.

findings.impact: The per-tick pre-grading scan and write-lock work can grow with unrestricted accumulated history. A fixed bounded-round guarantee and a bounded cancellation checkpoint cannot be established from this implementation.
not_claimed: No literal infinite loop is proved: a finite unchanged database has a finite collection.
No actual f7 history size, recovery duration, lock wait, worker exception or skipped grading tick was observed.
This static engineering gap is not established as the cause of either f7 browser failure.
findings.suggested_narrow_repair: Bound both selection and stop checks per tick, retain a durable or otherwise correct continuation over verified owner-scoped history, and preserve exact grade/binding/failure integrity checks and atomic recovery. Ensure grading receives its same-tick round after the bounded recovery slice. The concrete repair and regression test were not implemented or executed in this audit.
findings.title: The pre-grading evidence recovery scan has no fixed per-tick work bound or bounded stop checks on already-handled history
verified_static_evidence: EvidenceRecovery materializes every workspace in learning_submission_bases inside the default immediate transaction; the workspace query has no LIMIT.
completed_grade_keys materializes every matching completed grade as a tuple; the query has no LIMIT or per-tick continuation.
For each key already bound or recorded as a recovery failure, run_once executes a lookup and continues before checking stopping().
There is at most one newly processed recovery item, but its selection scan is not bounded by a fixed row/work budget; a no-work tick can scan all prior grades.
The same default BEGIN IMMEDIATE spans the scan and recovery work. Grading is called only after this method returns.

database_wait.evidence: The default sqlite connect timeout and PRAGMA busy_timeout are10000ms; transaction uses BEGIN IMMEDIATE unless immediate=false.
database_wait.interpretation: A potential single busy wait can exceed the observed late grading helper window. This is a source possibility, not a measured wait, cumulative duration or proof of lock contention.

evidence_recovery.dispatcher_consequence: ApiError with no import lease returns false from ImportWorker.run_once; sqlite3.Error reaches _loop and is converted to worked=false. Both paths skip this tick's later grading call; the loop then waits0.25s. Occurrence in f7 is NOT_OBSERVED.
evidence_recovery.item_savepoint_known_failures_isolated: ApiError/ValueError/TypeError/KeyError/sqlite3.IntegrityError inside the actual recovery item are rolled back and recorded, then the method returns true.
evidence_recovery.limitations: Policy and all downstream owner ports were not recursively expanded within the12-file cap; no particular policy error is asserted to have occurred.
evidence_recovery.pre_item_errors: completed_grade_keys catches only ASSESSMENT_ACTIVE locally. Another ApiError propagates; SQL/select/begin failures can also escape before the item savepoint.

grading_chain.queue_presence_short_circuit: NOT_PRESENT_IN_DISPATCH: maintenance booleans are combined only after grading and the import claim; a successful maintenance result alone does not skip grading

recommendations.active_assessment: Returnsfalse for ASSESSMENT_ACTIVE without computing a public recommendation.
recommendations.primary_known_error_isolation: PASS_STATIC: run_once catches ApiError,ValueError,TypeError,KeyError,sqlite3.Error, records a fixed failure/retry projection when possible, and returnsfalse. Its recovery recording catches the same group.
recommendations.prior_to_try: database.workspace_id() is called before the main try; initialization/connect errors there are not covered by this local handler. MigrationError is not a normal f7 occurrence claim.
recommendations.work_extent: _no_work and refresh call workspace-wide load_inputs and checked snapshots; the current file has no aggregate wall-clock budget. Not every transitive load/derive/port was expanded; no unbounded runtime or hang is inferred.

retrieval.compute_extent: compute loops through the frozen scope's block descriptors, checks stopping per block, uses separate short lease-renew/read transactions, and tokenizes outside the database transaction.
retrieval.dispatch_isolation: PASS_STATIC: parent catches ApiError/sqlite3.Error around retrieval.run_once and still reaches grading; damaged derived storage does not automatically skip grading for those groups.
retrieval.one_lease: run_once consumes one invalidation then may claim and fully compute one registered lease.
retrieval.other_errors: Not every possible exception class is covered by the local parent retrieval catch; none is observed in the supplied f7 diagnostics.
retrieval.resource_bound: Normative retrieval-resource-v1 bounds the accepted scope to512 blocks/16MiB registered body bytes. This review did not reread the entire transitive descriptor admission implementation and does not claim that the loop has a fixed millisecond budget.

grading_chain.simple_starvation_claim: Cannot reject all pre-grading delay/early-exit possibilities from source; cannot admit any as actual f7 cause without per-tick/claim evidence.

next_falsifiable_actions.action: Implement only a bounded recovery selection/continuation and test the real dispatch seam with many already-bound/failure history rows. Verify a fixed maximum scan slice, stopping checks, preserved exact recovery history, no repeated/omitted candidate recovery, and actual same-tick grading call. Source-level absence of a budget is resolved only by an explicit bound, not a faster machine or raised timeout.

Use a narrowly approved future diagnostic at actual recovery/recommendation/retrieval/grading tick boundaries and grading claim/result boundary to distinguish delay, error skip, eligibility guard and unobserved later completion. Preserve original command/assertions/timeout/retry. A trace showing all preceding stages finish promptly rejects this pre-grading-delay attribution for that execution; no trace was collected here.

A narrowly approved future same-owner observation of course JSON/metadata validation, lesson validation, block/body validation and open callback can distinguish pending transport/body parse, genuine contract mismatch, changed owner and successful open. A completed valid same-owner chain must reach existing open; headers alone cannot decide the outcome.
